title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. In insurance, paying 2x book for a 15% ROE underwriter works only if the cycle does not erode the denominator.
epigraph.author: Institutional Underwriting Maxim

web_blocks.html: On November 16, 2026, Chubb Limited closed at $381.28. That price equals 13.34x trailing EPS ($28.57), 12.88x forward EPS, and 1.99x reported book value per share ($191.43) [3, 26, 27]. Excluding AOCI bond marks, Chubb's book value per share was $201.31 at year-end 2025 (~1.87x on Q3 2026 ex-AOCI book of ~$204) [2, 3]. The stock trades above its 2016–2023 historical P/B range of ~1.27x–1.65x [30]. Meanwhile, commercial property pricing has shifted from hard-market expansion to active softening (-8% to -10%+ in large accounts) [9, 11].

A Justified Price-to-Book model shows what $381.28 prices in today. Using Justified P/B = (ROE - g) / (Ke - g) with a 9.5% cost of equity and 3.5% terminal growth, a 1.99x multiple implies a ~15.4% perpetual ROE. Chubb's actual TTM ROE is 15.48% [3]. On current Q3 2026 ex-AOCI book (~$204), a normalized 14.5% ROE yields 1.83x P/B, or $373.32 today. Why, then, is our 12–18 month Base Target $425.00? Because Chubb compounds ex-AOCI book value at ~12%–13% annually via retained earnings and buybacks, lifting FY2027E ex-AOCI book value toward ~$230; applying 1.85x to ~$230 yields $425.50 (13.9x FY27E EPS of $30.57).

web_blocks.takeaway: At $381.28, CB already prices in ~15.4% perpetual ROE—matching its TTM peak (15.48%)—leaving only ~11.5% upside to our $425 base target.

web_blocks.takeaway: CB trades at 13.34x TTM P/E and 1.99x P/B with a 15.48% ROE—richer on P/B than AIG (1.10x, 8.23% ROE) and ACGL (1.63x, 18.74% ROE), while cheaper than TRV (2.85x, 27.50% ROE) and PGR (3.98x, 33.24% ROE).

web_blocks.html: Post-Q3 2026 Wall Street targets cluster between $350 and $380 (for example, Morgan Stanley lifted its target to $380 with a Neutral rating) [26, 27]. Our 12–18 month Base Target of $425.00 offers +11.5% upside from $381.28. Against the $340.06 stop, CMP risk-reward is only 1.06:1, failing our 1.5:1 hurdle.

Peer comparisons on the November 16 ledger reinforce this discipline. Arch Capital (ACGL) trades at 9.06x TTM P/E and 1.63x P/B on an 18.74% ROE. Travelers (TRV) trades at 10.57x TTM P/E and 2.85x P/B on a 27.50% ROE. Chubb's 1.99x P/B already carries a quality premium, capping near-term multiple expansion.

Historical valuation bands confirm that Chubb's current 1.99x P/B sits near the top of its 10-year range [30]. Between 2016 and 2023, shares typically traded between 1.27x and 1.65x reported book value. Only during peak ROE cycles with 5%+ bond yields has the market paid near 2.0x book.

If commercial property rates continue softening through 2027, underwriting margins will likely normalize from 85.7% toward 87%–89%. Higher investment income offsets much of that normalization. Even so, multiple expansion from 1.99x P/B is unlikely without an unexpected hard-market rebound.

Dividend and buyback math also anchors long-term total return. Chubb pays a 1.04% dividend ($3.98 TTM, 14.88% payout ratio) and retired $3.39B in shares during FY2025 [2]. Combined with 7%–8% organic book-value compounding, normalized total return potential sits near 11%–12% annually from support. Buying at $381.28 compresses that first-year return cushion.

In addition, Chubb's 2016–2024 historical record shows why valuation discipline matters across cycles [29, 30]. In 2016, CB posted $28,145M NPW, an 88.7% combined ratio, and 10.5% GAAP ROE at ~$103.60 BVPS. By 2020, pandemic losses pushed the combined ratio to 96.1% and ROE to 6.2%. By 2024, hard-market pricing lifted NPW to $51,468M, combined ratio to 86.6%, and ROE to 15.0% [29]. Buying near 2.0x book at peak ROE leaves little cushion.

Valuation Upgrade Trigger: A pullback into $355.15–$370.85 (~1.74x–1.82x current ex-AOCI book) expands upside to our $425.00 Base Target to +14.6%–19.7%, clearing our 1.5:1 risk-reward hurdle against the $340.06 stop.

book_paragraphs: Now that you and I have spent six chapters inside Chubb's underwriting engine without once glancing at a ticker tape, it is time to lift the veil and look at what the market is charging for this franchise. On November 16, 2026, Chubb closed at $381.28—just three dollars shy of its 52-week high of $384.26—representing 13.34 times trailing earnings, 12.88 times forward earnings, and 1.99 times reported book value per share.

At first blush, 12.88 times forward earnings looks downright cheap next to an S&P 500 trading north of 20 times. Do not fall into that cross-sector trap. Insurance balance sheets are levered roughly three-to-one on equity through policyholder float, and book value is the true anchor of intrinsic worth. When we run the Gordon Growth identity—Justified P/B equals (ROE minus growth) divided by (Cost of Equity minus growth)—a 1.99x multiple with a 9.5% cost of equity and 3.5% terminal growth tells us the market is already underwriting a 15.4% perpetual return on equity. Chubb's trailing twelve-month ROE is 15.48%. In other words, Wall Street is paying peak-cycle multiples for peak-cycle profitability.

Compare Chubb side by side with its peers on the live November 16 ledger. Travelers trades at 10.57 times trailing earnings and 2.85 times book on a 27.50% ROE. Arch Capital trades at just 9.06 times trailing earnings and 1.63 times book on an 18.74% ROE. AIG trades at 1.10 times book because its ROE lags at 8.23%, while Progressive commands 3.98 times book for a 33.24% ROE. Chubb sits squarely in the quality-at-a-full-price middle: superior diversification and A++ balance sheet strength, but no longer a neglected bargain.

This is why price-blind underwriting matters so much. We know from Chapters 1 through 6 that Chubb is a legitimate COMPOUNDER_PASS business. Yet at $381.28, our $425 base target—13.9 times $30.57 of FY2027E EPS—offers only 11.5% upside against 10.8% downside to the $340.06 structural stop. Great businesses bought at 52-week highs with 1.06-to-1 asymmetry turn into mediocre 12-month investments. Let us turn to the technical tape in Chapter 8 to see where patience pays.

Let us look closely at the peer table in Chapter 7, because relative valuation keeps us honest. When you compare Chubb at 1.99x book and 13.34x trailing earnings against Arch Capital at 1.63x book and 9.06x trailing earnings, you immediately see that Chubb is no longer the discounted compounder it was three years ago. The market has recognized Chubb's 85.7% combined ratio and $6.95 billion investment income run-rate, and it has bid the stock up to $381.28.

Does that mean Chubb is wildly overvalued? Not at all—an 11.5% expected return to our $425 base target plus a 1.04% dividend yield is still solid. But as disciplined capital allocators, we demand at least 1.5:1 reward-to-risk before committing fresh money. At $381.28, we only get 1.06:1. Waiting for a 3% to 6% pullback into the $355.15–$370.85 support zone restores the exact margin of safety we require.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: THE PEAK-ROE MULTIPLE TRAP
book_callouts.text: The single most expensive mistake in P&C insurance investing is multiplying peak-cycle earnings by a mid-cycle multiple. At 1.99x book value, Chubb is priced for its 15.48% ROE to endure indefinitely—even as large-account commercial property rates fall 8% to 10%+.

book_subsections.title: Why 1.99x Book Value Leaves Zero Margin for Error at $381.28
paragraphs: Let us walk through the valuation math one step further so you can see why we refuse to chase at $381.28 even though we admire the business. Suppose Chubb earns $30.57 per share in FY2027—roughly 7% growth over its trailing $28.57 EPS, powered by higher bond yields and 4% annual share buybacks. If the market values Chubb at 13.9x forward earnings—already near the upper end of its 10-year historical band—the stock reaches $425.00.

From today's $381.28 close, $425.00 is +11.5% upside, or +$43.72 per share. Meanwhile, our technical invalidation stop sits just below the 30-week SMA at $340.06, which is -$41.22 per share (-10.8%). Divide +$43.72 by $41.22 and you get 1.06-to-1 reward-to-risk. Now run the exact same math if Chubb pulls back 3% to 6% into our $355.15–$370.85 support zone: at $370.85, upside to $425.00 jumps to +$54.15 against -$30.79 of risk (1.76:1). At the $363.00 midpoint, upside is +$62.00 against -$22.94 of risk (2.70:1). Same company, same target, completely different investment.

book_subsections.title: What Consensus Price Targets Tell Us About Expectations
paragraphs: After Chubb reported Q3 2026 core operating EPS of $7.66—crushing consensus estimates near $6.77—and record adjusted net investment income of $1.89 billion, Wall Street analysts raised their price targets into the $350 to $380 range. Morgan Stanley, for example, lifted its target to $380 while keeping a Neutral rating. Notice what that tells us: at $381.28, Chubb is already trading right at or slightly above the Street's post-earnings fair-value cluster.

Our own 12-to-18-month Base Target of $425.00 is more constructive than Wall Street's near-term range because we give Chubb credit for 5.5% bond reinvestment yields and ongoing share repurchases compounding FY2027E EPS toward $30.57. Even so, $425.00 from $381.28 is only 11.5% upside against 10.8% downside to our $340.06 stop. That is why we wait for the $355.15–$370.85 buy zone.

book_subsections.title: Understanding Book Value Ex-AOCI vs. Reported Book Value
paragraphs: One quick accounting tip before we move to the chart: always check both reported book value per share ($191.43) and book value per share excluding AOCI ($201.31 at year-end 2025, and roughly $204 in Q3 2026). Reported book value fluctuates every quarter with 5-year Treasury yields even when Chubb has zero intention of selling its bonds before maturity.

On reported book value, $381.28 is 1.99x; on ex-AOCI book value, it is roughly 1.87x. Either way, Chubb trades above its 10-year median valuation band, confirming that the market is already paying up for peak underwriting margins and 5%+ investment yields.
